text:
maria: thinking out loud — proposing we adopt a tenant-striping model for the console query layer so heavy tenants get pinned to their own query worker pools instead of noisy-shared lanes. reduces tail latency for large customers and simplifies isolation.
aj: curious — is this stripe-by-customer or stripe-by-traffic-shape? those are different complexity profiles.
kevin: +1 for striping by customer for enterprise tiers, but we should avoid O(number_of_tenants) worker explosion. prefer 'stripe-by-commitment' (reserved pools) for paid tenants and a pooled fallback for small ones.
sasha: two immediate concerns: RBAC enforcement when routing (we must preserve tenant-scoped auth filters) and cache invalidation scope (sharded caches mean more cache misses on cross-tenant queries).
maria: agreed. idea: routing key = tenant_id for pinned paths, else route based on hash(session_id) for pooled lane. RBAC stays as early filter on request proxy so routing happens after auth check.
aj: sounds ok. For cache: we can namespace caches by tenant shard id. That mitigates cross-tenant pollution but increases memory cost. We should estimate memory delta.
olivia: from the console UX side, we surface cost/latency per-tenant. If we pin heavy customers, dashboard telemetry will show stabilizing latency curves — helpful for SRE and sales.
kevin: implementation thought: introduce a Router interface with two strategies: "TenantStripe" and "AdaptivePool". Router returns target worker group and a cache namespace. Keep Router logic in control-plane; workers stay dumb.
sasha: agree on separation. also need an ABI contract: worker must accept requests with "cache-namespace" header and opaque tenant metadata so no auth logic leaks.
aj: migration plan? we can't cut over all at once. propose canary: pick 3 paid tenants, enable pinning in canary mode, measure tail p99/p95, ops cost.
maria: +1. add automatic fallback: if pinned pool CPU exceeds threshold, route overflow to pooled lane to avoid head-of-line blocking.
kevin: fallback rule needs circuit-breaker semantics and backpressure signals — prefer to emit slow-path metrics and let autoscaler decide.
olivia: question: how does this affect RBAC policy changes (e.g., tenant role revokes)? If you pin tenant to a long-lived worker, revokes must propagate quickly.
sasha: workers should subscribe to policy pubsub. control-plane publishes change with sequence id. workers check sequence id on request if last_seen < current -> refresh before serving.
aj: that adds a small perf hit on policy churn, but policy changes are rare. ok.
maria: action items:
- kevin: draft Router interface and wireframe for cache-namespace header (PR)
- sasha: estimate memory delta for tenant-namespaced caches and sketch pubsub refresh flow
- aj: canary plan doc with tenant candidates + SLOs to monitor
- olivia: update dashboard telemetry plan and sales comms note
- i'll file an RFC follow-up linking the implementation plan and migration timeline
kevin: can do. also will add simple simulation to estimate pool sizes vs #tenants.
olivia: pinging @deploy-bot to schedule a small canary infra sandbox next week? :calendar:
deploy-bot: scheduled "console-tenant-striping-canary" sandbox on 2043290000; infra creds and cluster link posted in #eng-platform-canaries.
maria: thanks everyone. leaning to start with reserved pools for enterprise + pooled fallback. we'll iterate after canary metrics. if anyone has objections, speak now or comment on the RFC follow-up.
aj: no objections from me. one follow-up: add latency budget per path (query vs projection) in canary metrics.
kevin: added to my PR checklist.
sasha: will add a short section on RBAC perf test in load tests.
olivia: I'll coordinate comms with support for flagged tenants.
maria: closing thread for now — RFC follow-up link will be in #eng-platform. :lock_with_ink_pen:
